=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal_intake.sh:3334-3349 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: `_heal_build_suspect_commits` passes `PROVENANCE_DEFAULT_BRANCH` (the intake/self repo's default branch, set at intake.sh:1261-1265) as `--default-branch` while querying `--repo "${SOURCE_REPO}"`, which can be a consumer repo; unlike the divergence compare (line 2923) and `_heal_run_reproduction` (line 3070), it has no `SOURCE_REPO == SELF_REPO` guard.
  WHY: For a consumer stall/timeout report with regression=true, the slow-day `repos/<consumer>/commits?sha=<self-default-branch>` query either 404s and is wrongly logged as `partial/slow_day_commits_failed`, or lists commits from a non-default branch as suspects; the documented outcome is `partial/default_branch_unavailable` (all reviewers rated it MAJOR).
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py:6787-6995 | severity=high | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The compare GET (line 6995) sets no pagination, yet `parse_suspect_compare` takes `parsed[-SUSPECT_COMMITS_MAX:]` (line 6812) and `render_suspect_commits_section` captions it "newest {len(commits)} shown" (line 6886), even though the API returns commits oldest first and returns only one page (at most 250).
  WHY: When the last-green...failing range is larger than one page, mid-range commits are labelled as the newest suspects and the commits closest to the failing SHA are missing, which misleads the heal plan; agents.d/heal-suspect-commits.md repeats the "newest 15" claim. Severity disagreement: sonnet rated it NIT; minimax, luna and glm rated it MAJOR.
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py:7050-7053 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The new keyword parameter `suspect_commits` of `compose_issue_body` shadows the new module-level `def suspect_commits(` (line 6915).
  WHY: This breaks the §10 new-identifier-uniqueness rule, and any later call to `suspect_commits(...)` inside `compose_issue_body` would raise TypeError (`_cmd_compose_issue` already avoids the clash with `suspect_commits_text`). Severity disagreement: gemini rated it MAJOR; sonnet, minimax and glm rated it NIT.
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py:9667-9671 | severity=low | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: In the `_cmd_suspect_commits` OSError branch, if `--out` is written but the `--files-out` write fails, the summary becomes `partial/helper_failed` but keeps non-zero counts; the intake (`_heal_build_suspect_commits`, intake.sh:3350-3367) then logs the full-key form and still attaches section.md.
  WHY: The agents.d/heal-suspect-commits.md registry (line 5) says `helper_failed` appears alone and does not list it among the `partial` reasons, so log scanners keyed on the documented shape will mis-parse it, and the attached section contradicts the failure signal (all reviewers rated it NIT).
- agents.d/heal-suspect-commits.md:2 | severity=low | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The fragment says that with the switch off the intake "makes no call, writes no file and logs no line", but the `jq -n ... > "${HEAL_LAST_GREEN_CACHE_FILE}"` write at scripts/workflow_failure_heal_intake.sh:3102-3103 is gated only by the reproduction path, not by `WORKFLOW_HEAL_TREND_ENABLED`.
  WHY: The issue body and API calls are still byte-identical, but the "writes no file" claim is false, so the documentation contradicts the code (both rated it NIT).
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py:6986, 6143-6145, 6084-6092 | severity=high | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: When `before` is empty (run-info has no parseable `created_at`, intake line 3332), `last_green_run` omits the `created=<` bound and `parse_last_green_run` skips the `newer_than_failure` check, so a green run newer than the failure can become the baseline; the cache-hit path (line 6981) also gets no fresh check.
  WHY: The compare then comes back `behind` with `ahead_by=0`, so the section silently renders "0 commits" and names no suspect, which hides the real cause (minimax rated it MAJOR; sonnet and glm raised the same issue only as hardening suggestions).
- tests/test_review_autofix_provider_outage_contract.py:121-127 | severity=critical | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The pre-push gate reports `test_label_contract_and_reporter_skip` as failing, so the PR is not gate-green.
  WHY: The failure blocks a green gate (possibly sandbox staging or cross-test pollution); glm notes the assertion reads intake.sh regions this PR does not touch, so the cause is not visible in the diff. Severity disagreement: gemini rated it BLOCKER (confidence 5), glm rated it NIT (confidence 2).
- tests/test_workflow_checkout_integration_ref_audit.py:N/A | severity=critical | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The pre-push gate reports a failure in tests/test_workflow_checkout_integration_ref_audit.py.
  WHY: The failure blocks a green gate; glm notes the audit reads only `.github/workflows/*.yml`, which this PR does not modify, so the cause is not visible in the diff. Severity disagreement: gemini rated it BLOCKER (confidence 5), glm rated it NIT (confidence 2).
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal_intake.sh:3317 | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  PROBLEM: printf writes trend_json to `${trend_dir}/summary.json` non-atomically and suppresses failures with `|| true`.
  WHY: A partial or empty summary.json can make the downstream suspect-commit step fail or skip unnecessarily (NIT).
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal_intake.sh:3263 | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: In `_heal_build_run_time_trend`, `printf '%s' "${trend_json}" > "${trend_dir}/summary.json" 2>/dev/null || true` is a non-atomic write and swallows errors.
  WHY: A torn or empty summary.json makes `_heal_build_suspect_commits` emit `skipped reason=shape_unknown`, which silently disables suspects for that report and cannot be told apart from a non-stall shape (NIT; same root cause as the gemini item at line 3317, but the line numbers differ, so it is kept separate).
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py:6778 | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The `".." in filename.split("/")` check uses substring containment per segment, so legitimate filenames such as `scripts/v1.0..2.0-check.sh` are silently dropped from the pipeline files list.
  WHY: A real pipeline file changed in the range is left out of the `## Suspect commits` evidence with no truncation marker; a segment-equality check would keep the traversal defence (NIT).
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===
- requirement: "The first-slow-day commits call is made only when `regression=true`." plus "skipped with `reason=default_branch_unavailable` when the default branch is unknown; it never falls back to `main`" (agents.d)
  expected_change_site: scripts/workflow_failure_heal_intake.sh `_heal_build_suspect_commits` lines 3334 and 3349
  confidence=4
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  EVIDENCE: For consumer reports (`SOURCE_REPO != SELF_REPO`), the intake still forwards `PROVENANCE_DEFAULT_BRANCH` as `--default-branch` with no same-repo guard (the reproduction step has one at line 3070), so the result is `partial/slow_day_commits_failed` instead of the documented `default_branch_unavailable`.
- requirement: "Fail open, logging `WORKFLOW_HEAL suspect_commits outcome=partial reason=<r>`." and "`partial` with `reason=no_last_green|compare_failed|malformed|slow_day_commits_failed|default_branch_unavailable`" (agents.d line 5)
  expected_change_site: scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py `_cmd_suspect_commits` lines 9667-9671 and scripts/workflow_failure_heal_intake.sh `_heal_build_suspect_commits` lines 3357-3365
  confidence=4
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  EVIDENCE: When the `--files_out` write fails, the summary keeps the full keys while outcome/reason flip to `partial`/`helper_failed`, which contradicts the "helper_failed alone" contract; the read failure has a handler (`WORKFLOW_HEAL warn suspect_commits_unreadable`) but the write failure has none.
=== END CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal_intake.sh:3334 (`_heal_build_suspect_commits`, `suspect_default_branch=`) | severity=MAJOR | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: `PROVENANCE_DEFAULT_BRANCH` is the intake repo's default branch (intake.sh lines 1261-1265) but is passed as `--default-branch` for `--repo "${SOURCE_REPO}"`, which can be a consumer repo (line 1272); unlike lines 2923 and 3070, there is no same-repo guard.
  WHY: A consumer trend with regression=true either 404s and is logged as `partial reason=slow_day_commits_failed`, or lists the wrong branch's commits as suspects; fix: set the branch only when `SOURCE_REPO,,` equals `SELF_REPO,,`.
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py (`parse_suspect_compare`, `render_suspect_commits_section`, compare GET in `suspect_commits`) | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The unpaginated compare returns commits oldest first and may return fewer than `total_commits`, yet the tail is captioned "newest N shown"; agents.d/heal-suspect-commits.md repeats "newest 15".
  WHY: For long ranges, mid-range commits are shown as the newest and the commits nearest the failing SHA are missing; fix: record `total > len(raw_commits)` and adjust the caption.
- agents.d/heal-suspect-commits.md:2 vs scripts/workflow_failure_heal_intake.sh `_heal_run_reproduction` lines 3102-3103 | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The `HEAL_LAST_GREEN_CACHE_FILE` write is gated by reproduction, not by `WORKFLOW_HEAL_TREND_ENABLED`, so "writes no file" is false.
  WHY: Nothing user-visible changes, but the documented contract is false; fix: gate the write on `TREND_ENABLED` or correct the sentence.
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py `_cmd_suspect_commits` OSError branch; consumer intake `_heal_build_suspect_commits` | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: If `--out` succeeds and `--files-out` fails, the helper exits 0 with `partial/helper_failed` and non-zero counts; the intake logs the full form and attaches section.md.
  WHY: This contradicts the agents.d registry (`helper_failed` alone); fix: use a distinct reason such as `files_write_failed`, or clear the section.
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py `compose_issue_body(..., suspect_commits: str | None = None)` | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The parameter shadows the new module-level `def suspect_commits(`, which breaks §10.
  WHY: A future call inside the function would raise TypeError; renaming is cheap now.
- HARDENING: scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py `suspect_commits`, the `last_green_run(..., before=before or None, ...)` call: with `before` empty, the baseline can be newer than the failure, so the compare comes back `behind` and is reported as `ok` with 0 commits; fix: return `partial/no_last_green` on status `behind` or on a falsy `before` without a cache (2-3 lines).
- HARDENING: scripts/workflow_failure_heal_intake.sh `_heal_build_suspect_commits` line 3334: `[ "${SOURCE_REPO,,}" = "${SELF_REPO,,}" ] || suspect_default_branch=""` (1 line). HARDENING_RISK_SCORE: 2
